stakeholder_role: Engineering tooling lead choosing one unsupervised coding assistant to generate Python bug-fix drafts on a team's SymPy codebase before human code review.
population: Single-issue SymPy bug reports paired with maintainer regression tests: source pool from SWE-bench Verified SymPy instances (issues 2016-2023); target pool from SymPy PRs created and merged with all closing issues created on or after 2026-05-01T00:00:00Z.
fit_criterion: Without internet access or oracle leakage and without modifying any test runner or test configuration file, the agent's patch cleanly applies to the base commit and passes every maintainer test that checks behavior stated in the bug report, within 900 seconds. Removing tasks with confirmed B05 or B07 test defects implements this fit criterion directly rather than revising the requirement.
text: Working alone in a local SymPy checkout without network access or test-runner modifications, the coding agent resolves bug reports by passing maintainer tests that check stated bug-report behavior, with one-sided 95% exact binomial lower bound at least 0.70 within 15 minutes per bug report.

decision_rule_spec.accept_condition: One-sided 95% exact binomial lower bound >= 0.70 (P(X >= k | n, 0.70) <= 0.05)
decision_rule_spec.reject_condition: One-sided 95% exact binomial upper bound < 0.70 (P(X <= k | n, 0.70) < 0.05)

n_min_reason: Smallest sample under exact one-sided 95% binomial bounds where Accept is possible: 9/9 gives upper-tail p = 0.0404 <= 0.05 (8/8 gives 0.0576 > 0.05).
values_note: 70% matches the study threshold carried from earlier protocols so an assistant solves roughly seven of ten issues without setup; 15 minutes (900 s) is the unattended run budget per ticket before human takeover. Neither value was empirically calibrated from a field productivity study.

sample_size.note: Protocol 6 sizes at 44 source and 44 post-cutoff target tasks per agent (178 active + 20 reserve = 198 max slots) as approved by the author. At N=44 under one-sided 95% exact binomial cut points (Accept >= 37, Reject <= 25), Accept power at true rate 0.85 is 66.3% before removal and 49.4% at n=31 (30% removal), below the 80% design target which required 60 retained (75 starting) tasks; exact power across N in {31, 44, 52, 60, 75} is reported.

controlled_policy_history: POLICY-P6-CONTROLLED was defined on 2026-11-11 after Protocol 5's signed forms returned No decision (failing B12, B14a, B14b, and release-level B28a) and before any Protocol 6 agent session.

CONFIG_01_GEMINI_FLASH_MED.justification: The source tasks and the target tasks come from the same repository and are the same kind of work: a bug report on SymPy, a change to SymPy's source code, and tests that the maintainers wrote with the fix. People screened the source tasks for clear issue text and fair tests (SWE-bench Verified). The pull requests that fix the target issues were merged from 2026-06-13 to 2026-11-05, after Gemini 3.8 Flash's stated training cutoff (March 2026, as stated in its model card, which adds that for some domains the model's knowledge is limited to January 2025). If the stated cutoff holds, the fixes were not in its training data. Five target issues were opened before the cutoff, so the agent may have seen their text. The agent gets the same instructions, tools, and 15 minutes for both kinds of task, and in each the Python version that the task's own grading uses (3.9 for the source tasks, 3.12 for the target tasks).
CONFIG_01_GEMINI_FLASH_MED.limits: The source issues are older (2016 to 2023), SymPy's code has changed since, and the target tasks run on a newer Python. The target issues were not screened by people. The screened source tasks may be easier than typical issues. The agent may have seen the source tasks' fixes in training (B14). The method checks only that this justification exists, names its author, and matches the scope; it does not judge its content. The stated cutoffs are the providers' claims, not checks.
